summary_html: Agency places a child with **relatives or kin caregivers** instead of non-relative foster care. Federal law favors kinship care as least-restrictive, family-preserving placement.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The SJC affirmed the Juvenile Court judge's choice of the parents' plan for adoption by a paternal aunt over the department's plan for adoption by the foster mother, holding that the judge owes an even-handed assessment of competing plans and that his decision is entitled to substantial deference.
key_cases.relevance: Hugo is the leading Massachusetts authority for a court preferring a relative caregiver's plan over the agency's non-relative plan.
key_cases.quote: A judge should provide an “even handed” assessment of all the facts surrounding both the department’s plan and any competing custody or adoption plan.

key_cases.holding: The SJC held that a guardian who is a de facto parent has no liberty interest supporting a procedural due process right to counsel in a removal proceeding, but that the Probate and Family Court's equitable powers permit a judge to appoint counsel for an indigent guardian where the child's best interests warrant it.
key_cases.relevance: K.N. governs the legal position of a kin or de facto caregiver whose guardianship the agency or a parent later seeks to undo.
key_cases.quote: A guardian who is a de facto parent does not have a liberty interest in her relationship with her ward sufficient to warrant the appointment of counsel.

key_cases.holding: The Appeals Court affirmed judgment for the Commonwealth and for the individual social workers on a former foster child's claims arising from her placement with a man who abused her, holding among other things that the workers had qualified immunity because the asserted right to safety in a relative placement was not clearly established at the time.
key_cases.relevance: Sheila S. is the Massachusetts decision analyzing agency liability for placing a child with a purported relative without verifying his circumstances.
key_cases.quote: The plaintiff’s placement with a relative, rather than in foster care, further supports the conclusion that she has not asserted a right that was clearly established.

key_cases.holding: The SJC affirmed the finding that the mother was currently unfit by clear and convincing evidence but vacated the order committing the three sisters permanently to the department and remanded, because the judge's findings failed to address the importance of the sibling relationship and whether placing all three children with their paternal grandparents would serve their best interests.
key_cases.relevance: Three Minors is the source of the Massachusetts sibling-togetherness preference that Willow and Zander apply, and it requires findings on a proposed kinship placement of all the siblings together.
key_cases.quote: The courts of this Commonwealth have recognized the importance of siblings' being raised together.

key_cases.holding: The SJC affirmed a Probate and Family Court judgment awarding the father custody of his daughter but ordering continuing visitation between the child and the maternal aunt who had been her guardian and de facto parent, holding that the judge's reliance on the child's best interests was appropriate and fell within the court's general equity jurisdiction notwithstanding the absence of any statute authorizing visitation for an aunt or former guardian.
key_cases.relevance: Youmans establishes that a kin caregiver who has become the child's de facto parent may be given court-ordered continuing contact even after custody passes to a legal parent.
key_cases.quote: The judge's consideration of Tamika's best interests was entirely appropriate.

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Emergency order transferring custody (DCF must file the care and protection petition on the next court day after taking emergency custody, M.G.L. c. 119, § 51B(c))
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: An emergency order transfers custody for up to 72 hours only; custody continues past 72 hours solely if the court so determines after notice to the parents, guardian or custodian (M.G.L. c. 119, § 24)

timeline_requirements.deadline: 45 days for the department or agency to provide a copy of the service or case plan to the parent, guardian or custodian and to the attorneys for all parties appearing in the proceeding
timeline_requirements.starts_from: The department or agency filing an appearance in the proceeding (M.G.L. c. 119, § 29)

timeline_requirements.requirement_name: Appointment of counsel for indigent parent
timeline_requirements.deadline: 14 days for the juvenile court and probate and family court departments, under procedures they must establish, to appoint counsel for an indigent parent, guardian or custodian
timeline_requirements.starts_from: A licensed child placement agency filing or appearing as a party in the action (M.G.L. c. 119, § 29)
